markdown.headingText: Why not build a custom quiz app?
markdown.markdown: Students answer these quizzes **on their own phones** during class, after scanning a QR code. This page explains how it works and how to set one up for a new session. A live, whole-class quiz needs a server that collects everyone's answers in real time and shows them on a shared screen. This website is a **static site** (just files, no server), so instead of building and hosting that infrastructure, we use a free existing tool for the live part, and the website only holds the **QR code / link** that points students to it. ## Choosing a tool | Tool | Best for | Notes | |---|---|---| | **Google Forms** | Quick checks, homework-style quizzes, results you can review later in a spreadsheet | Link is **permanent** — create it once, embed the QR code in the site, reuse every year | | **Kahoot** | Fun, competitive, live-projected quizzes with a countdown timer | Each session gets a **new game PIN** — can't be baked into the static site in advance | | **Wooclap / Socrative** | Similar to Kahoot, plus open-ended and word-cloud question types | Same PIN/session-code limitation as Kahoot | **Recommendation:** use **Google Forms** for the quizzes linked from this website (permanent QR code, zero setup on class day), and reach for **Kahoot/Wooclap** separately, live, when you want a projected, competitive, in-the-moment quiz — just display their join screen instead of using this site. ## Setting up a Google Forms quiz (once per session) 1. Go to [Google Forms](https://forms.google.com) → new form → click the **Settings gear → Quizzes** → turn on "Make this a quiz". 2. Add your multiple-choice questions and mark the correct answer for each (so students get instant feedback). 3. Click **Send** → the **link (🔗) icon** → copy the short link. 4. Open the session's `index.qmd` file and replace `REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_GOOGLE_FORM_LINK` (it appears **twice**: once in the image `src`, once in the "Or open the quiz directly" link) with that link. 5. Re-render the site (`quarto render` or `quarto preview`) — the QR code image updates automatically, because it's generated on the fly from the link you pasted (via [api.qrserver.com](https://api.qrserver.com), a free public QR-code service — no software to install). That's the whole reusable pattern — the block below is what's in each session page: ````markdown ::: {.qr-block} ::: {} **Quiz title — N questions** 1. First question, just as a reminder of what's being asked 2. ... [Or open the quiz directly →](YOUR_LINK_HERE) ::: ::: ```` ::: {.callout-note} If you'd rather not depend on an external QR image service, you can generate a QR PNG offline with the `qrcode` Python package (`pip install qrcode[pil]`) and reference the saved image file instead of the `api.qrserver.com` URL — the rest of the block stays the same. ::: ## Reusing your existing exam questions Your `EXAM/exercises/*.Rmd` files (written for the R/exams package, used for the paper exam) are a ready-made question bank. Each file has the question text and a `TRUE`/`FALSE` solution vector for the answers — that maps directly onto a Google Forms multiple-choice question. For example, `Einstein_L1_Q1.Rmd`, `Q2` and `Q3` became the three questions used in the [Scientific Method quiz](sessions/02-scientific-method/index.qmd). When building out the remaining sessions, pull 2–4 questions per session from the matching `Einstein_L*_Q*.Rmd` files as a starting point for that session's live quiz.
